hints: Focus on what the two given test results tell you, 2,4-DNPH and Tollens, to pin down the exact functional group first.
Deduction / Stepping Stone: Positive Tollens means aldehyde, so with formula C3H4O acrolein must be CH2=CH-CHO, containing both C=C and -CHO.
Synthesis / Final Link: Now test each statement against that structure, checking for the iodoform group, reducibility to a primary alcohol, and addition to a double bond.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional group from the tests**

Great start, let the observations do the work. A positive 2,4-DNPH test means a carbonyl compound, aldehyde or ketone.

A positive Tollens test (silver mirror) narrows it to aldehyde only.

**Work out the structure of acrolein**

Molecular formula is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_4\text{O}$. As an aldehyde it must contain $-\text{CHO}$.

That leaves $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3$ which fits a $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond: $$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$$ This is propenal, commonly called acrolein.

**Check statement 1, iodoform test**

Alkaline aqueous iodine gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ only with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})-$ groups.

Acrolein has $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-$ and $-\text{CHO}$, no methyl carbonyl group, so statement 1 is false.

**Check statements 2 and 3 and conclude**

Reduction of an aldehyde with e.g. $\text{NaBH}_4$ or $\text{LiAlH}_4$ gives a primary alcohol: $$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$ So statement 2 is true.

The $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond undergoes electrophilic addition and decolourises orange bromine water to colourless, so statement 3 is true. Only 2 and 3 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 2 and 3 are correct but statement 1 is false because acrolein lacks the CH3CO- group needed for the iodoform reaction.
options.B: Incorrect. This claims 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 2 is correct but statement 1 is false, and statement 3 is also correct and is missing here.
options.C: Correct. Statement 1 is false (no iodoform group), statement 2 is true (aldehyde reduces to primary alcohol CH2=CH-CH2OH), and statement 3 is true (C=C decolourises bromine water). So 2 and 3 only are correct.
options.D: Incorrect. This claims 1 only is correct. Statement 1 is actually the false one, as CH2=CH-CHO cannot form CHI3 with alkaline iodine.
